minutes.headline: Board approved special permits for a Flat Hill Road home rebuild and a Summer Street used-car lot capped at 50 cars
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard two special-permit applications: a demolition and rebuild of a single-family home at 922 Flat Hill Road on a non-conforming lot, and a used-car dealership proposed for 40 Summer Street. Both were approved, the car lot capped at 50 vehicles pending the applicant working with police and fire on site access and paving. The board also read and accepted a longtime member's resignation letter and noted openings for associate members before adjourning.

votes.motion: Motion to approve the special permit for the 922 Flat Hill Road demo/rebuild application
Motion to grant the special permit for the 40 Summer Street used-car dealership for 50 cars, provided police and fire authority obtained and conditions maintained

decisions.decision: Board asked the car-lot applicant to check with the fire and police departments about emergency vehicle access before the lot is finalized.
Applicant agreed to pave the unpaved portion of the Summer Street lot to fit the cars and comply with police/fire access, though it may take about five months.
Board settled on a 50-car cap for the dealership rather than the 70 originally requested, after discussion of past caps granted at that site (35, then 60 contingent on paving that was never done).
Board to accept applications (via the town job bank) for two open associate seats on the Zoning Board of Appeals.

what_happened.line: Board approved a special permit for a used-car dealership at 40 Summer Street, capped at 50 vehicles rather than the 70 requested.
Cap and prior conditions were set after the board noted a past 60-car allowance at the site was contingent on paving that was never completed.

Approval requires the applicant to work with police and fire on emergency vehicle access before the lot is finalized, and to pave the unpaved portion, which the applicant said could take about five months.
Board separately approved a special permit for a demolition and rebuild of a single-family home at 922 Flat Hill Road on a non-conforming lot.
Board accepted a member's resignation and opened applications for two associate seats.

why_it_matters: A commercial special permit with a vehicle cap and access conditions affects traffic and emergency response on Summer Street, and the town will need to confirm the paving and police/fire sign-off actually happen before the lot operates at full capacity.
The Flat Hill Road approval lets a non-conforming residential lot be rebuilt, a path other owners of older, non-conforming lots may look to as precedent.
Two open associate seats on the board are now accepting applications through the town's job bank.
